Laura / team — first pass below. I kept the language concise and focused on limiting operational burden while addressing reasonable customer assurance needs.

Suggested contract edits (high level):
1) Audit/Inspection Rights: Replace broad language with: "Customer may request evidence relating to Redwood's SOC 2 Type II report and supporting control summaries. Customer inspection rights shall be limited to (a) review of Redwood's SOC 2 Type II report; and (b) one on-site or remote inspection per twelve (12) month period, provided Customer gives no less than thirty (30) days notice and the scope is mutually agreed in writing. Any inspection that would require access to customer-specific data must be scoped and scheduled separately with appropriate narrowness and customer consent."

2) Penetration Testing: Add explicit operational constraints: "Customer may conduct or engage third-party vendor for penetration testing on Redwood systems used to serve Customer's environment no more than once per 12 months; Redwood must be given thirty (30) days written notice and the test must be limited to non-production or pre-authorized staging environments. Redwood will provide a post-test remediation summary; full vulnerability reports that include Redwood internal remediation plans may be redacted to protect security posture and third-party vendor IP."

3) Evidence Cadence: Propose: "Redwood will provide (i) the most recent SOC 2 Type II report within ten (10) business days of request (subject to NDA where applicable), and (ii) a quarterly assurance summary (one page) outlining control changes and outstanding remediation items. Other artifacts (control matrices, architecture diagrams) will be shared on a mutually agreed cadence and limited to information reasonably necessary to demonstrate compliance."

4) Data Handling / Redaction: Add a clause that Redwood may redact internal metrics, non-customer-specific operational telemetry, and any vendor-provided IP from artifacts prior to sharing.

These proposals aim to keep the agreement prescriptive but limited. If Fidelity insists on broader rights, suggest we negotiate a short addendum for larger enterprise deals with clear SOW and scheduling constraints.

I'll prepare a marked-up redline for the MSA/order form and attach. Priyom — please add operational feasibility notes (e.g., what we can commit to in the quarterly summary and what requires manual pulls).

-Karthik
